title: What if there isn't another 10x? Why growth isn't the only path for a mature company
summary: Jason Cohen argues that no company 10x's forever, and that tech's obsession with growth multiples eventually stops being the right question. Once a business has likely peaked, he says its true impact comes from applying its success to betterment (jobs, working conditions, community) rather than only biggerment.

principles.text: Asking "how do we 10x?" suits a young startup but cannot remain the right question forever.
principles.quote: "How do we 10x" is a great question when a startup is young. Does it always remain the right question?

principles.text: No company grows 10x forever; even Google responds by becoming a conglomerate of separate companies that could each 10x.
principles.quote: At some point it cannot be the right question. No company 10x's forever. Not even Google.

principles.text: The tech industry overweights growth in valuation, even when a slower-growing company produces far more cash profit.
principles.quote: Nevermind that Microsoft created more cash profit in 2015 than Facebook made in revenue.

principles.text: If another 10x isn't plausible, redirect attention to employees, communities, and using your infrastructure for something important.
principles.quote: how could you be redirecting your attention to other important things, like creating more jobs and better working conditions, to be a catalyst for employee's personal growth, to give back to relevant communities

principles.text: Ploughing everything back into 10x growth isn't optimal for making your dent in the universe; true impact is set when you turn to betterment.
principles.quote: it is at that moment, when a company is applied to betterment instead of (only) biggerment, that the nature of a company's true dent in the universe is determined.

principles.text: Expanding beyond a core product is hard: Dropbox, OpenTable and Yelp may simply be excellent at one thing, not platforms for everything.
principles.quote: What if Dropbox is just an awesome file-sharing and backup service but not a universal key/value storage API and native document format?
